definition: A virtuoso is a performer of dazzling, masterly skill — one whose command of an art, especially music, goes far beyond ordinary competence.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word virtuoso. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know virtuoso should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By the second encore even the stagehands had crowded into the wings to watch the virtuoso, a cellist who made the concerto's impossible passages sound like breathing.
Competent is far milder than virtuoso: competent playing hits the right notes and keeps the tempo, while a virtuoso commands the instrument so completely that the hardest passages sound easy.

Masterly is strong but still sits below virtuoso: masterly playing shows full command of the craft, while a virtuoso adds the dazzle — difficulty dispatched so brilliantly that audiences come just to watch it done.

Maestro is a title of authority — the revered master, most often the conductor or teacher the whole orchestra defers to. A virtuoso is named for the playing itself: the dazzling command an audience can hear. A maestro may never touch an instrument all evening; a virtuoso earns the word mid-performance.

A prodigy astonishes early — talent arriving so young it seems unearned, and the word says nothing about polish. A virtuoso's mastery is finished and trained, judged by the performance rather than the birthday. A ten-year-old prodigy may grow into a virtuoso; the second word has to be earned.
